exact_statement: For every finite-valued s:N->[0,infinity) with s(N)=o(N), let K_E(s) be the supremum B(F)/I(F) over all finite N-bit Boolean signs satisfying 0<I(F)<=2^(-s(N)), with B=sum_i H(S_i|S_-i) in bits and ordinary influence. Then K_E(s)=K_E in the extended reals. For any nonconstant seed f, h_m=z*f^(tensor m) is balanced, B(h_m)=mB(f), I(h_m)=mI(f)+1; its point activation obeys B(F_m)>=2^(-k_m)*mB(f) and I(F_m)=2^(-k_m)*(mI(f)+1+k_m), with k_m=o(m) chosen for the s-class. Consequently C_FEI<=K_E(s)+2/ln2 by C018. This is aggregate-erasure transport and does not preserve a selected coordinate witness. Finiteness of K_E(s) remains open.
hypotheses: Uniform finite Boolean signs; all dimensions; entropy in bits
Aggregate B, not selectable-coordinate min ratio
Suprema and equality interpreted in extended reals

exact_statement: For every fixed integer ell>=2 and every finite-valued s:N->[0,infinity) with s(N)=o(N), define R_geell(F)=sum_i sum_(T subset [N] minus {i}, |T|>=ell) phi(Fhat(T)^2,Fhat(T union {i})^2), where phi(x,y)=(x+y)h2(y/(x+y)) in bits with continuous zero conventions. The supremum K_geell(s) of R_geell(F)/I(F) over all finite N-bit Boolean signs with 0<I(F)<=2^-s(N) equals K_E=sup_(all finite nonconstant Boolean f) B(f)/I(f), in the extended reals. For every actual seed f and integers m,k>=1, let h=chi_Z*f^tensor(m) on ell fresh parity bits, F=1+A_k(h-1), q=2^-k, with all blocks disjoint. Then B_data(F)=qmB(f), I(F)=q(mI(f)+ell+k), R_geell(F)=qmB(f)+kq+2kq^2 sum_(r=ell..k-1) binom(k-1,r), and R_ge2(F)=qmB(f)+2kq(1-kq). Each parity coordinate z has B_z(F)=0 and Inf_z(F)=q>0, so min_(i relevant) B_i(F)/Inf_i(F)=0. No finiteness of K_E or selected-witness transport is asserted.

exact_statement: For every finite Boolean seed f, every m,k>=1 and ell>=2 on disjoint uniform blocks, let h=chi_Z product_b f_b, J=mI(f)+ell, F=1+A_k(h-1), q=2^-k, d=(1-q)^2+q^2. For each relevant coordinate use mu_i(T)=p_(T+i)/Inf_i and r_i(T)=p_T+p_(T+i); both normalize to one. Let M=sum_i Inf_i[log2(1/Inf_i)-D(mu_i||r_i)] and D_f be the KL divergence of the normalized joint derivative/reference laws, with I(f)D_f=0 for constants. Original core-coordinate divergences obey D_i(F)=D_i(h)+k, D_i(h)=D_i(f) on seed blocks and D_i(h)=0 on parity bits. Every control divergence is D_c=(1-q)(k-1)+q log2(q/d). Consequently I(F)=q(J+k), I(F)D_F=q[mI(f)D_f+kJ+kD_c], M(F)=qmM(f)+k[q(1-q)+q^2 log2(d/q^2)], and M_ge2(F)=qmM(f)+kq(1-kq). For every fixed ell>=2 and finite nonnegative s(N)=o(N), the supremum of M_geell/I over 0<I<=2^-s(N) equals the unrestricted supremum K_M in the extended reals. No finiteness of K_M, universal refund payment or full FEI conclusion is asserted.

exact_statement: For all Boolean G(s,X),H(s,Y) with one shared fair physical bit s, disjoint private uniform blocks X,Y and a fresh fair selector z, and normalized complete finite-cost references R_G,R_H, calibrate each reference separately on the two atoms empty and {s} to the true Fourier probabilities and rescale its complement. Costs c_G^c,c_H^c do not increase; the exact decrease is the categorical KL of those two atoms and the complement. The normalized compatible reference Q=rK, r=(R_G^c+R_H^c)/2 and K the actual conditional selector spectrum with a fixed normalized kernel on zero true fibers, has zero posterior mismatch kappa and D(P_F||Q)=[D(P_G||R_G^c)+D(P_H||R_H^c)]/2. Its complete cost is CE_F=(c_G^c+c_H^c)/2+Delta<=(c_G^c+c_H^c)/2+(2+4/ln2)Inf_z(F), where F=(G+H)/2+z(G-H)/2, Delta=B_z+J_z and I(F)=[I(G)+I(H)]/2+Inf_z(F), including s only through its actual averaged influence. Thus supplied child bounds transfer with constant max(K_G,K_H,2+4/ln2). For a t-bit shared block the same constant holds if both conditional-mean Fourier vectors have l1 norm <=1; without that hypothesis a proved coefficient is 2+(2*2^(t/2)+2)/ln2. No absolute selector-only coefficient holds for unrestricted sharing: selecting the even-k quadratic bent sign and its actual singleton flip has Inf_z=2^-k and Delta/Inf_z>=k-log2(16/9) for every even k>=4. This is a scoped reference transfer and an actual Boolean obstruction to its unrestricted selector-only extension, not a disproof of FEI.
